summary.text: The strongest convergent signal in ulcerative colitis mucosa is the neutrophil-recruitment axis of CXCR2, CXCR1 and their ligand CXCL8. CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking: it is raised in all five biopsy cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264]), local to inflamed mucosa, genetically supported in Open Targets and has clinical-stage antagonists, none approved in UC. Single-cell data place almost all CXCR2 transcripts in neutrophils and composition adjustment removes most of its bulk change, so the axis reads first as a marker of neutrophil influx and only secondarily as a target on recruited neutrophils.

The candidates that hold up best as tissue-level targets are those whose increase survives composition adjustment in a replicated cell of origin: CHI3L1 and MMP1 in inflammatory fibroblasts, DUOX2 in enterocytes and IDO1 in myeloid cells and epithelium. OSMR, the stromal oncostatin M receptor, is the only leader that combines genetic support with a clinical antibody (vixarelimab), but most of its bulk rise tracks composition. CHI3L1 is the most consistent expression change and is tractable but has no genetic support and no drug.

The most reproducible biomarkers are the loss of epithelial metabolic and barrier genes (CLDN8, HMGCS2, AQP8), down in all or nearly all cohorts, and the gain of neutrophil and antimicrobial genes (S100A8, AQP9, CXCL8, DUOX2, LCN2). Some changes are local to inflamed mucosa (CXCL8, HMGCS2), whereas others are already present in non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients (CLDN8, CHI3L1, SERPINB5) and may mark the disease state itself.

TNFa, NFkB and JAK-STAT pathway activity and STAT3 transcription-factor activity are raised in all five cohorts; these axes are already targeted by approved UC drugs and act as positive controls, as do IL12B, JAK2, TNF and S1PR1 in Open Targets. In the trial cohorts, baseline TNFa activity, CXCR2, TREM1, CHI3L1 and OSM are higher in ustekinumab non-responders but also in placebo non-responders or without a drug-by-placebo interaction, so they mark severity rather than drug-specific resistance; baseline IL23A and ITGB7 do not stratify response to the drugs that block them.

As first-in-class hypotheses, the discovery screen proposes SDR16C5, an epithelial (goblet and transit-amplifying cell) gene whose increase is largely intrinsic and replicated in five cohorts, and CPXM1, an inflammatory-fibroblast gene; both are antibody-tractable with low vital-organ expression but lack functional data in colitis.

expression.text: The random-effects meta-analysis across the five cohorts identifies a large, reproducible inflammatory program. The strongest consistent increase among the convergence leaders is CHI3L1 (pooled log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.71], padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=4.8e-33]), significant upward in every cohort.

Alongside CHI3L1, the up-regulated program is dominated by neutrophil chemokines and receptors (CXCL8, CXCL1, CXCR2, CXCR1), calprotectin (S100A8, S100A9), antimicrobial and oxidative epithelial genes (DUOX2, DUOXA2, LCN2, REG1A) and stromal metalloproteinases (MMP1, MMP3, MMP7), together with IDO1 and SERPINB5. SLC6A14 has the largest pooled increase of all (log2FC [gene=SLC6A14; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=5.02]) but is measured in four cohorts with very high heterogeneity (I2 [gene=SLC6A14; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; i2=0.982]), so its size is uncertain. Approved UC targets change little in comparison: TNF (meta log2FC [gene=TNF; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.74]) and ITGB7 (meta log2FC [gene=ITGB7; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.41]), so the size of a transcript change is not a measure of therapeutic value.

The decreased genes describe loss of differentiated colonocyte function: the tight-junction gene CLDN8 is the strongest decrease (meta log2FC [gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.52]), followed by the water channel AQP8 (meta log2FC [gene=AQP8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.31]), the gluconeogenic PCK1, the glucuronidase UGT2A3, the ketogenic enzyme HMGCS2 (meta log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.58]) and the sulfate transporter SLC26A2. These are robust biomarkers of epithelial injury and metabolic failure rather than drug targets.

inflammation.text: Comparing inflamed and non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients separates local from background changes. CXCL8 is a pure marker of local inflammation: the non-inflamed vs control contrast is flat (log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0037], padj [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.986]) while the paired inflamed vs non-inflamed contrast is strongly positive (log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.97]).

HMGCS2 shows the same local pattern on the down side: normal in non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.065], padj [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.675]) and falling in inflamed vs paired non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.95]), so epithelial metabolic loss follows local inflammation.

CLDN8, by contrast, is already lost from non-inflamed mucosa (non-inflamed vs control log2FC [gene=CLDN8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-1.60], padj [gene=CLDN8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=9.66e-14]), a barrier change present beyond the inflamed segment that may mark the disease state itself.

CHI3L1 combines both patterns: the non-inflamed vs control contrast is already positive (log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.84]) and the paired inflamed vs non-inflamed contrast adds a further rise (log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.62]).

DUOX2 behaves similarly: a rise in inflamed vs paired non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.48]), with non-inflamed mucosa already showing a smaller rise (log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.81]).

SERPINB5 has the most significant meta-analysis result among the leaders (padj [gene=SERPINB5; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=4.81e-135]); non-inflamed mucosa already shows a rise (log2FC [gene=SERPINB5; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=1.04]), and its low neutrophil share ([gene=SERPINB5; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.05]) makes it a tissue change.

OSMR is mainly a local change: a rise in inflamed vs paired non-inflamed mucosa (log2FC [gene=OSMR; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.88]) with only a small non-inflamed vs control shift (log2FC [gene=OSMR; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.18]). The paired increase of IDO1 (log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.68]) is also local.

replication.text: The discovery cohort's leading changes reproduce well in the four microarray cohorts: every leading convergence gene except CCL2 changes in the same direction in all five cohorts. CXCL8, for example, replicates everywhere (meta padj [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=5.27e-17]) and is largest in the small Leuven infliximab cohort (log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; log2fc=7.21]), a reminder that array fold changes are compressed and cohort sizes differ, so directions and significance are compared, not magnitudes.

REG1A is the clearest partial replication: up in four cohorts but not significant in the Leuven infliximab cohort despite a large fold change there (padj [gene=REG1A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.132]).

CCL2 has data in only four cohorts and a modest paired inflamed vs non-inflamed rise (log2FC [gene=CCL2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.74]), so its convergence rests on genetics and a phase 2 antibody more than on expression.

literature.text: Literature support in the corpus is mostly biomarker-level and mechanistic. Calprotectin transcripts (S100A8 with S100A9) are associated with endoscopic disease and proposed as diagnostic markers, HMGCS2 is reported decreased in UC with diagnostic value, and CXCL1 and MMP1 appear in bioinformatic diagnostic signatures; DUOX2 is among the most elevated proteins in inflamed UC biopsies in a proteomic study. Mechanistic single studies report that CHI3L1 promotes macrophage pyroptosis via BCAT1/NF-kappaB and that IDO1 drives M1 macrophage polarisation, with an IDO inhibitor protective in mouse colitis; the axis of CXCL8 with CXCR1 and CXCR2 is described as participating in UC pathogenesis. None of these is a clinical trial.

The literature is silent where other streams are strongest. CXCR2, first in the ranking, has no verbatim-validated UC literature relation in the corpus and rests only on the Open Targets literature score ([gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; literature=0.7203]); published UC evidence for CXCR2 blockade is thin here.

OSMR likewise has no extracted UC relation and a low Open Targets literature score ([gene=OSMR; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; literature=0.1311]) despite genetic support.

The only CHI3L1-directed compound in the corpus is velpatasvir, which binds recombinant CHI3L1 with micromolar affinity in a repurposing study, so CHI3L1 has mechanistic but not pharmacological validation.

external.text: Approved UC targets appear as positive controls in Open Targets: IL12B heads the list (association [gene=IL12B; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7424]), with JAK2, TNF and S1PR1 also near the top. JAK2 has strong genetic support (genetic association [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8458]) yet a small biopsy change (meta log2FC [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.87]), and S1PR1 is one of the few approved targets that also rises clearly in biopsies (meta log2FC [gene=S1PR1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.20]).

Among expression-led leaders, genetics supports CXCR2 (genetic association [gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.8171]), FCGR2A ([gene=FCGR2A; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; genetic_association=0.87]), IL2RA, OSMR, CCL2 and CD274. CXCR2 has clinical antagonists (reparixin up to phase 3, navarixin, ladarixin and SX-682 in phase 2), OSMR an antibody-tractable profile with vixarelimab in phase 2, CCL2 the antibody carlumab and IL2RA approved antibodies such as basiliximab, none approved in UC. FCGR2A has no drug. CD274 drugs block PD-L1, the wrong direction for colitis, so CD274 is a marker of interferon-driven inflammation, not a target.

The strongest expression changes mostly lack genetic support. CHI3L1 has a low Open Targets association ([gene=CHI3L1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.1136]) and no drug, but predicted antibody and small-molecule tractability; UniProt describes it as a secreted lectin that drives AKT1 activation and IL8 production in colonic epithelial cells.

IL1B (canakinumab), IDO1 (epacadostat, linrodostat) and MMP9 (andecaliximab) have clinical drugs from other indications but no genetic association with UC; IDO inhibition is immune-activating, so its direction for colitis is uncertain, and the stromal MMPs that lead on expression have only broad-spectrum inhibitors. STRING places CXCR2 at the hub of the ELR+ chemokines CXCL8, CXCL1, CXCL5 and CXCL2, which are themselves among the leaders.

cells.text: Single-cell data separate tissue targets from markers of cell influx. In the Gubatan dataset, which captures neutrophils, CXCR2 transcripts are almost entirely neutrophil (share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]); in Smillie, which lacks neutrophils, the residual lineage call does not replicate. After composition adjustment CXCR2 keeps only a small part of its bulk increase (retained [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.17]).

CXCL8 is mostly neutrophil (share [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]) and loses significance after adjustment (adjusted padj [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0527]), the only leader with a full composition verdict. CXCR1, AQP9, S100A8, S100A9, OSM, IL1B, FCGR2A and CD274 are also neutrophil-dominated, so their bulk rises largely reflect neutrophil influx. Because lineage scores rise when resident cells activate, the adjustment can over-correct: losing significance is not proof of pure influx.

CHI3L1 is made by inflammatory fibroblasts (Smillie share [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.652], stromal lineage replicated), with a neutrophil contribution in Gubatan, and keeps a significant change after adjustment (adjusted log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.40], padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=1.63e-16]): a tissue change of activated stroma, not only influx.

DUOX2 is epithelial (lineage share [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947], replicated), expressed by most inflamed enterocytes ([gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.pct_expressing=77.7%] of cells), and keeps a significant adjusted change (padj [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=1.83e-9]): an intrinsic epithelial response.

MMP1 comes from inflammatory fibroblasts (Gubatan share [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed_with_neutrophils.0.share=0.681]) and keeps a significant adjusted change (adjusted log2FC [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.26]).

OSMR is stromal (lineage share [gene=OSMR; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.907], replicated), led by inflammatory fibroblasts, but retains only part of its bulk change after adjustment (retained [gene=OSMR; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; retained_fraction=0.222]), which may reflect over-correction of activated stroma.

IDO1 is myeloid in Smillie (lineage share [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.598], replicated) while enterocytes make the largest share in Gubatan, and it keeps a significant adjusted change (adjusted log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.85]).

LCN2, often read as a neutrophil marker, is made almost entirely by non-neutrophil cells (neutrophil share [gene=LCN2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.043]), i.e. an epithelial antimicrobial response.

pathways.text: TNFa, NFkB and JAK-STAT pathway activity is raised in all five cohorts (TNFa t in UNIFI [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=20.07]; JAK-STAT t in MSCCR [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=15.68]), together with STAT3 ([type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=24.0] in UNIFI), NFKB1 and AP1 transcription-factor activity. These axes are already targeted by approved UC drugs (anti-TNF, JAK inhibitors) and act as positive controls; STAT3 is also the shared node of IL-6/gp130 and OSM signalling.

Untargeted pathways are equally active: TGFb has the largest t in UNIFI ([type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=25.17]) and EGFR, MAPK, hypoxia, PI3K and VEGF are up in all five cohorts, so broad activation does not discriminate mechanisms. Not every pathway is robust: p53 is lower in only three cohorts (Leuven infliximab t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE16879.t=-3.59]), WNT is not significant in GSE73661 (padj [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE73661.padj=0.0637]) and Androgen is mixed. The epithelial TF HNF4A is inconsistent (PURSUIT t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE92415.t=-4.61]) despite the loss of epithelial metabolism genes.

Among specific circuits, the strongest is CXCL8 from Neutrophil CXCR4 to Neutrophil via CXCR2, stronger in inflamed than uninflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755]): an autocrine/paracrine neutrophil recruitment loop addressed by clinical CXCR2 antagonists but by no approved UC drug. The neutrophil OSM to LP fibroblast circuit via IL6ST is weak, scoring lower in inflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709]) with only a Neutrophil PADI4 pair appearing from a zero baseline, and macrophage IL1B pairs mainly with the decoy receptor IL1R2 on neutrophils (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.168]), which may be buffering rather than signalling. Co-expression is not proof of signalling.

treatment.text: Higher baseline TNFa pathway activity is associated with non-response to ustekinumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]), infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.000294]), vedolizumab and golimumab, but also with placebo non-response in UNIFI (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]), so it marks severity. TGFb behaves the same way (UNIFI placebo padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00984]). JAK-STAT is associated with ustekinumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) and infliximab non-response but not vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]), with a borderline placebo arm (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0543]).

Baseline OSM is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]) and not significantly in the UNIFI placebo arm (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]), but the drug-by-placebo interaction is null (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.971]) and no other drug arm survives correction, so there is no evidence of a drug-specific OSM effect.

CXCR2 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) and in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]), with no interaction: neutrophil burden marks severe disease regardless of drug.

TREM1 follows the same severity pattern (ustekinumab BH padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]; UNIFI placebo padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]).

CHI3L1 separates UNIFI placebo non-responders even more than ustekinumab non-responders (placebo difference [gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).diff_nr_minus_r=1.575], BH padj [gene=CHI3L1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0203]), a severity marker rather than a marker of drug-specific failure.

Target expression does not stratify response to the drug that blocks it: baseline ITGB7 is not associated with vedolizumab response (BH padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]).
Likewise, baseline IL23A is not associated with ustekinumab response (BH padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]).

discovery.text: SDR16C5 is the strongest first-in-class hypothesis. It is up in five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.55]), keeps most of its increase after composition adjustment (retained [gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.66]), is epithelial (lineage share [gene=SDR16C5; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.918], replicated; goblet and transit-amplifying cells lead), antibody-tractable and has low vital-organ RNA ([gene=SDR16C5; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=26.9] nTPM). What is missing: any functional evidence in colitis, a protein-level confirmation and a reason why a retinol dehydrogenase would be accessible to an antibody.

CPXM1 is a stromal hypothesis: inflammatory fibroblasts lead its expression (share [gene=CPXM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.213]; lineage replicated), it is up in five cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.64]) and partly composition (retained [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.41]), with low vital-organ RNA ([gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=9.1] nTPM). It would fit the inflammatory-fibroblast program that also makes CHI3L1, MMP1 and OSMR, but its function in the gut is unknown.

XKR9 has the highest retained share after adjustment ([gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.80], epithelial) but is up in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=2] cohorts, so it fails the replication standard and is not carried forward.

LAX1 tops the discovery list by fold change (meta log2FC [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; meta_log2fc=1.79]) but keeps little of its increase after adjustment (retained [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.23]) as a T/NK gene, so it likely reflects lymphocyte influx.

ADGRG3 passes the filters and is tractable by antibody and small molecule, but its transcripts are neutrophil (share [gene=ADGRG3; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; neutrophil_share=0.906]), making it a neutrophil target rather than a tissue one.

PCDH17 retains almost none of its increase after adjustment (retained [gene=PCDH17; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.098]), the weakest tissue-intrinsic evidence among the discovery hits.

CHRDL2, a stromal hit, has the highest vital-organ RNA among the leading discovery candidates ([gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6] nTPM), a safety point to check before any development.

integration.text: Expression, replication, genetics and tractability converge most fully on CXCR2 and CXCR1, which are the only leaders with all six evidence streams and clinical antagonists; but the cell stream shows them to be neutrophil genes whose bulk change is mostly influx, and the treatment stream shows CXCR2 to mark severity in placebo arms as well. The second point of convergence is the inflammatory fibroblast: CHI3L1, MMP1, OSMR and the discovery candidate CPXM1 share this cell of origin, keep part of their change after composition adjustment and replicate across cohorts, while TGFb, the pathway most associated with fibroblast activation, is active in every cohort and untargeted.

The streams disagree in three places. Genetics supports JAK2, FCGR2A and CXCR2 but the strongest expression changes (CHI3L1, DUOX2, MMP1, SERPINB5) have no genetic association; approved targets (TNF, ITGB7, IL23A) change little in biopsies and their baseline expression does not stratify response; and the literature corpus is silent on CXCR2 and OSMR, the two leaders with genetic support and drugs, while it describes CHI3L1, IDO1 and DUOX2 mechanistically. The convergence ranking rewards drugs and genetics, so it ranks neutrophil receptors first; weighting cell of origin and composition moves CHI3L1 and the stromal program ahead as tissue targets.

targets.rationale: Ranked first by judgment although eighth numerically: the most consistent increase in all five cohorts, made by replicated inflammatory fibroblasts and keeping a significant change after composition adjustment (a tissue change), tractable by antibody and small molecule, with mechanistic literature on macrophage pyroptosis. Against it: no genetic support, no drug, and it marks severity in placebo arms, so it is also a strong biomarker.

The only leader combining genetic support, a clinical antibody (vixarelimab) and a replicated stromal cell of origin (inflammatory fibroblasts); its ligand OSM is made by neutrophils. Moved up from its numeric rank because it is druggable on resident cells, but its bulk change is partly composition and the neutrophil OSM to fibroblast circuit is weak in single-cell data.

First in the convergence ranking with all six streams: up in five cohorts, local to inflammation, genetic support and clinical antagonists up to phase 3. Moved down because almost all its transcripts are neutrophil and most of its bulk change is influx, so it is a target on recruited neutrophils, not on tissue, and it marks severity in placebo arms.

An intrinsic epithelial change: up in five cohorts, made by inflamed enterocytes in both single-cell datasets and keeping a significant change after adjustment; protein-level literature support. No genetics or drug, so a mechanism of epithelial oxidative stress and a biomarker more than a ready target.

Inflammatory-fibroblast metalloproteinase, up in five cohorts, replicated cell of origin and a significant adjusted change; only broad-spectrum MMP inhibitors exist and literature support is bioinformatic.

Up in five cohorts, myeloid and epithelial origin with a significant adjusted change, clinical inhibitors and mouse data; but no genetic support, and IDO inhibition is immune-activating, so the therapeutic direction is uncertain.

Positive control: second Open Targets UC target with strong genetics and approved JAK-pathway drugs, and JAK-STAT activity is raised in all five cohorts; its own transcript change is small, which is why it ranks lower numerically.

The clearest marker of local inflammation: flat in non-inflamed mucosa, up in inflamed mucosa and in all five cohorts, but mostly neutrophil and fully explained by composition after adjustment, so a biomarker of neutrophil influx rather than a target.
Calprotectin subunit, up in five cohorts, neutrophil-derived and linked in the literature to endoscopic disease: a positive control for biomarker discovery (faecal calprotectin).
Strongest decrease in the meta-analysis and already lost in non-inflamed mucosa, marking barrier injury beyond the inflamed segment; a biomarker, not a target.
Loss of colonocyte ketogenesis in five cohorts, local to inflamed mucosa and supported by the literature as a diagnostic marker: a biomarker of epithelial metabolic failure.

Exploratory: first-in-class epithelial candidate with an intrinsic, five-cohort increase, replicated cell of origin, antibody tractability and low vital-organ expression; no functional data in colitis.
Exploratory: first-in-class inflammatory-fibroblast candidate up in five cohorts with low vital-organ expression, partly composition; function in the gut unknown.

limitations.text: This is the single-agent arm: one agent did the work of six specialists with fewer tool calls per stream, so coverage of genes per stream is narrower than in the multi-agent analysis.

Bulk biopsy transcriptomes mix cell types; the composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells activate, so losing significance after adjustment is not proof of pure influx, and shares in single-cell data compare cell types, not tissue abundance.
Microarray fold changes are compressed relative to RNA-seq and cohort sizes differ widely; directions and significance are compared across cohorts, not magnitudes.
Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression and pathway or TF activities are inferred from target genes; neither proves signalling.

Treatment associations are baseline associations with response, not predictions; the infliximab, vedolizumab and PURSUIT placebo arms are small and have little power, and golimumab results did not survive correction for any gene examined.
The literature corpus is a few hundred UC abstracts; absence of a relation is not absence of published work, and drug stages come from Open Targets and do not imply efficacy in UC.
